data.taskBrief:
TASK BRIEF: Create a PagerDuty incident and page the on-call engineer (PagerDuty)

FIT
  Fully. The supplied PagerDuty Events API request triggers an incident using the service integration routing key, which pages the configured on-call responders. No requests were dropped.

AUTH
  Bearer token authentication is configured by the collection fallback: send `Authorization: Bearer <bearerToken>`. The bearer-token value is unresolved in the supplied variables. The PagerDuty service integration credential is also supplied in the JSON body as `routing_key`.

BASE URL
  https://events.pagerduty.com

STEPS
  1. POST /v2/enqueue
     Params (JSON body):
       routing_key: string — `your-routing-key`; the PagerDuty service integration key
       event_action: string — `trigger`; use `trigger` to create/page an incident
       payload.summary: string — `Rule triggered alert`; concise incident description
       payload.source: string — `logicloop`; source of the event
       payload.severity: string — `critical`; incident severity
     Headers:
       Accept: string — `application/json`
       Content-Type: string — `application/json`
       Authorization: string — `Bearer <bearerToken>`
     Returns:
       202 Accepted; JSON body with `status` (string, shown as `success`) and `message` (string, shown as `Event processed`).
     Threading:
       None

GOTCHAS
  - Replace `your-routing-key` with the exact PagerDuty service integration key; it is required to route the event to the correct service.
  - Send the nested payload as valid JSON with `Content-Type: application/json`; do not flatten the `payload` object.
  - The URL is the resolved `pagerDutyIntegrationUrl` value: `https://events.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue`.
  - The collection references `{{bearerToken}}`, but no value for that variable was supplied. Confirm whether the target endpoint requires the configured Bearer header; the request body’s `routing_key` remains the PagerDuty event credential.
  - Use `event_action: trigger` to create a new incident. PagerDuty may deduplicate or attach rapidly repeated events according to its event-processing behavior.
